title: region-aware-onprem-networking-walkthrough
content:
Purpose: iterative operator-facing walkthrough for setting up VPC+regional affinity and KMS/HSM bindings in on-prem/private deployments. This is a working doc for product + applied-ml + SE to align on a single-screen flow that supports: per-region CIDR previews, key alias selection, HSM attestation hints, and a dry-run network validation step.

High-level goals:
- Make it obvious which regions will host control plane vs. compute (affinity toggle, visual map)
- Prevent common networking mistakes (overlaps, reserved ranges, missing routes) with immediate validation and remediation suggestions
- Surface KMS vs HSM tradeoffs early: cost/latency/attestation and step-through for operators to attach keys and schedule rotation
- Provide a repeatable dry-run that simulates traffic routing and fallback to hosted variants when capacity is constrained

Audience: platform engineers, customer SREs, solutions engineers installing Private in customer VPCs or air-gapped data centers.

Quick scenario (operator journey):
1) Start: select deployment target -> on-prem cluster A (region EMEA-1), add another region for redundancy (APAC-3).
2) Network sketch stage: operator drops in CIDR blocks for each region. UI runs immediate checks and highlights: 
   - CIDR overlaps with existing corp ranges (red highlight, suggested alternate range)
   - Missing NAT routes for model pull (actionable hint + one-click docs link)
   - No public egress allowed (toggle to enable/disable egress and list consequences)
3) Region affinity map: simple cards showing per-region capacity, latency estimate (derived from previous benchmarks), and preferred models. Operator can pin a model family to a region and the UI shows impact on token-cost and latency.
4) KMS/HSM step: two columns — "KMS (cloud)" vs "HSM (customer-managed)". For HSM path: guide includes attestation checklist and a minimal sequence: register HSM -> upload CSR -> validate attestation -> bind key alias. For KMS path: show IAM roles, bucket access, and example policy snippet to copy.
5) Dry-run validation: runs a simulated topology test and emits a short summary with severity levels. Also provides a downloadable diagnostic bundle (network trace, config snapshot, model routing plan).

Wireframe notes (desktop layout):
- Left column: stepper (Network -> Regions -> Keys -> Review -> Dry-run) with compact status badges (ok/warn/error).
- Center: main canvas with region map + CIDR overlays; mouse-over reveals subnet details and validation hints.
- Right: contextual panel with quick remediation suggestions and links to runbook fragments (copyable CLI commands, terraform snippets).
- Footer: "launch smoke tests" button (disabled until dry-run passes) and an "export config" dropdown for artifacts: terraform, helm values, config yaml.

Micro-interactions to consider:
- CIDR input: inline validator that suggests next available /24 range in that AZ if conflict detected
- HSM attestation: modal that accepts a base64 attestation blob and shows parsed metadata (vendor, firmware version). If parsing fails, show guidance and attach step to create support ticket automatically
- Region affinity toggle: sliding scale (0-100) to weight traffic distribution; tooltip that computes estimated token cost delta in real time

Failure modes and UX signals (important):
- If KMS policy denies access during binding: show exact failing policy line and the minimum permission set to fix (do not show full policy by default)
- If network dry-run times out: surface last successful checkpoint and a one-click re-run with verbose logs turned on
- When HSM attestation fails intermittently: offer retry + time-based backoff and record attempts in operator-visible audit trail

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we allow multiple HSM vendors in a single deployment? (pro: flexibility; con: added complexity for attestation UI) [decision needed: product + security]
- Should we include an "auto-assign" CIDR mode for busy customers who want minimal input? (Would need to ensure no overlap with corporate ranges)
- How deeply do we tie model routing suggestions to historical performance telemetry for customers who already run Redwood hosted? Privacy implications if we surface aggregated telemetry across customers.

Edge-case checks we want in dry-run (non-exhaustive):
- Asymmetric routing (ingress on region A but egress on region B) -> warn and show traffic path diagram
- Datacenter NAT gateway capacity below threshold -> warn and suggest smaller batch sizes or pull scheduling
- Key rollover scheduled in 24h -> show potential short window of degraded decrypts and recommended quiesce steps

Short snippet: sample HSM binding flow text to display in UI (concise)
1. Register HSM identifier (vendor serial)
2. Upload attestation blob (PEM/base64)
3. Confirm vendor fingerprint and firmware.
4. Create key alias and attach to deployment.
5. Schedule rotation (optional).

Developer notes / implementation pointers:
- Network validation: reuse existing infra validation service (ENG-1899) but add a lightweight client for dry-run that can be containerized and run inside customer's environment (airgap plan)
- Key binding: backend API should accept an attestation blob and return a normalized attestation object; UI shows only high-level fields to avoid vendor-specific noise
- Telemetry: record the sequence of operator actions as an event stream for replay in support tools (opt-out by default for privacy)

Next steps (short-term):
- Proto: build an HTML/CSS static mock of the main canvas + stepper — assign to Jonah (FE) for 2-week spike
- Backend: Miguel to spin up an API contract for attestation ingestion (ENG-1899) and validate with Priya on data model
- SE playbook: create a 1-pager with common failure modes and copyable fixes (target: 3 page doc)
- Schedule 1 customer dry run with internal staging cluster to capture real user feedback (target date: 2026-03-05)

Notes to self:
- Keep language in UI operator-first and prescriptive ("Fix this X to continue" vs. passive errors).
- Avoid overwhelming operators with full policy dumps — prefer minimal actionable lines and link to full logs for advanced users.

References and context links:
- ENG-1899: network dry-run service rewrite
- CON-4572: compliance checklist for customer-managed keys
- Slack thread: #private-deployments - thread id 5643 (notes from last customer onboarding)

Unresolved items to track in the ticket backlog:
- UX copy for HSM attestation states (pending legal/security review)
- Auto-CIDR mode algorithm proposal (engineering feasibility study)
- Readout from first customer dry-run and adjustments to cost estimates in region affinity panel

End of doc. This is intentionally iterative — expect sections to be trimmed and moved into separate PRDs once core flow is validated by the FE spike.
